svg.title: Amber plan vs HAEO's min-SoC reserve: 28 Oct midday trade and tonight
svg.desc: Three panels. Top: home battery SoC actual, the Amber 17:41 plan forecast, and HAEO's min-SoC target history and forecast. Middle: Amber import and feed-in prices, actual and plan forecast. Bottom: zoom 12:30-15:10 of actual grid power under Amber against HAEO's shadow-plan grid target.
svg.text: Amber plan vs HAEO's min-SoC reserve: 28 Oct midday trade and tonight
28 Oct 06:00 → 29 Oct 08:00 AEST · Remote EMS off (Amber V2X in control) · HAEO solving in shadow, not in control · BESS 40.3 kWh
contingency ≈ 7.4 kWh for the 05:00 peak or a spike
Amber plan: empty in the 20:30 interval,
Amber actual: export 19.3 kW for 25 min
HAEO shadow plan (blue): no export at 12:30–13:30; the battery only covers the house (3–7 kW)
HAEO import spikes at 13:30/13:45/14:10/14:20 are refill plans after Amber had drained the BESS
Selling 1 kWh at 19.4 c under HAEO's own costs: 1.08 kWh out of the BESS (98.7 % × 93.5 %), refilled at 14.6 c via 98 % × 98.7 %
= 16.3 c, plus 4 c wear → about −1 c/kWh, so HAEO holds. At Amber's 1 c wear it is about +2 c, so Amber sells,
then refills only 70 % and plans the BESS to 0 % tonight.
Sources: sigen_plant_battery_state_of_charge · haeo_battery_min_soc_target · amber_v2x plan · haeo_grid_import/export_target_kw · sigen grid power
